subject: Private endpoint: VPC/on‑prem firewall & egress playbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint: VPC/on‑prem firewall & egress playbook

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this on. As we prepare the Private deployment (VPC / on‑prem) for your sandbox and eventual prod environments, we need to lock down the allowlist and egress policy so your security/compliance team can sign off. High level asks from Acme (and from our side):

- Private endpoints for Redwood control plane (customer-managed) must only accept ingress from your VPCs via the listed private IP ranges / peering connections; no public EIPs to the control plane.
- Egress from your private environment must be restricted to a small set of Redwood service endpoints (token exchange, model fetch, telemetry) and to KMS endpoints for key wrapping. No general internet access for inference nodes.
- Firewall policy (per-zone): default deny, allow by application-tag for: SSH (restricted jumpbox CIDRs), TLS to Redwood endpoints, NTP, and DNS to approved resolvers.
- Audit requirements: we need flow logs (VPC flow logs / on‑prem FW logs) for 90 days, and a retained list of egress IPs.

I've attached our suggested baseline (redwood-private-egress-requirements.pdf) and an exemplar allowlist CSV for the minimal MVP (mvp-allowlist.csv). Could you share:
  - The CIDR ranges for your peered VPC(s) and any colo subnets you plan to use?
  - Your preferred DNS resolver IPs and whether DNS over TLS is required?
  - Which KMS/HSM endpoints you'll use (cloud KMS or on‑prem HSM)?

Proposed next steps: we draft a firewall rule snippet your NetOps can copy, then run a quick smoke test with a canary instance. Target: signoff by end of week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Platforms | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: VPC/on‑prem firewall & egress playbook

Marissa —

Thanks for the checklist. Quick answers below and attached our current FW policy draft (acme-fw-policy.docx).

- Peered CIDRs: 10.10.0.0/16 (prod), 10.11.0.0/16 (staging), colo subnet 172.20.100.0/24 (restricted).
- DNS: We use internal resolvers 172.20.200.10 and 172.20.200.11. Acme requires DNS over TLS for external resolution; internal lookups remain plain.
- KMS: We manage keys in a customer‑managed Cloud KMS (us‑west‑2). We also have an HSM in colo for high‑value signing workflows — we can provide IP ranges for the HSM mgmt plane.

We expect no general outbound internet from inference hosts. Allowed egress should be limited to:
- redwood-control.redwood-inference.com (TLS to specific FQDNs)
- model artifact S3 buckets in us‑west‑2 (signed URLs)
- Cloud KMS endpoints in us‑west‑2
- NTP & internal DNS

I've uploaded a network diagram here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-acme-network-diagram

Let me know if you want us to open a temporary tunnel for the model fetch test.

—Jordan
Jordan Pike
Sr. Director, Infrastructure | Acme Payments
jordan.pike@acme-payments.com

Attachments: acme-fw-policy.docx
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: VPC/on‑prem firewall & egress playbook

Jordan —

Appreciate the details. A few engineering clarifications / proposals:

1) Allowlist granularity
- We prefer IP ranges for the control plane plus FQDN allowlisting for model artifact fetch where signed URLs are used. If you can provide the S3 prefix(s) we can pin exact object stores.

2) Firewall snippets (example rule set)
- Inbound to control plane (from Acme VPC): allow TCP 443 from 10.10.0.0/16, 10.11.0.0/16, 172.20.100.0/24 -> destination redwood-control-private (internal LB).
- Outbound from inference nodes: allow TCP 443 to (a) redwood-control.redwood-inference.com resolved IPs, (b) aws kms endpoints (kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com resolved IPs), (c) specific S3 IP ranges if you require it.
- Block 0.0.0.0/0 outbound except for the above and NTP/DNS.

3) NAT & egress path
- If inference hosts sit in private subnets behind NAT, we need stable egress IPs for your firewall policies. Suggest using a small, dedicated NAT pool (e.g., 3–5 EIPs) per environment so flow logs are attributable.

4) Logging
- We'll need VPC flow logs (or equivalent FW logs) with at least 90 days retention. We'll also produce request-level telemetry for a 30‑day rolling window.

5) Test plan
- Can we start with a staging canary: 1 GPU instance in 10.11.0.0/16 that attempts to reach model fetch endpoints and KMS? We can do a 4‑hour smoke window.

I've pasted a small firewall example below you can hand to NetOps: 

--- begin snippet ---
# Allow incoming from Acme VPCs to Redwood control plane
ALLOW tcp 443 FROM 10.10.0.0/16 TO redwood-control-private
ALLOW tcp 443 FROM 10.11.0.0/16 TO redwood-control-private
ALLOW tcp 443 FROM 172.20.100.0/24 TO redwood-control-private

# Outbound from inference nodes
ALLOW tcp 443 FROM inference-subnets TO redwood-control.redwood-inference.com (resolved FQDN/IP list)
ALLOW tcp 443 FROM inference-subnets TO kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
ALLOW udp 123 FROM inference-subnets TO ntp.internal.acme
DENY ip FROM inference-subnets TO 0.0.0.0/0
--- end snippet ---

If you confirm the NAT pool approach, we can coordinate an update window with NetOps.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: VPC/on‑prem firewall & egress playbook

All —

We’re aligned on the approach. A couple of compliance notes from my side: 

- SOC2 / audit: we need to confirm the mechanism for providing the flow logs to Acme and for storing any logs that contain customer IPs. We typically provide an S3 bucket with restricted access (log-exports.acme-prod) — confirm if that meets your audit requirements.
- Temporary tunnel: for the initial model fetch test, a short-lived VPN (site‑to‑site) is acceptable if NetOps prefers that to modifying prod NATs during the smoke window. Tunnel must be limited to the staging CIDR and torn down automatically after testing.
- Canary & rollback: set a canary window (4 hours) with health checks against latency and token error rates. If errors > 1% or latency > 1.5x baseline we rollback and gather packet captures.

If NetOps can provide contact and a preferred change window, we’ll own the canary orchestration from Redwood.

Rishi
VP, Platform Reliability | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

2) Priyom: prepare the exact FQDN → IP resolution list for our control plane and the S3 prefixes we will use; draft the final firewall ruleset for NetOps copy/paste.
3) Rishi: prepare the log export S3 bucket policy template we can use for Acme audit ingestion.
4) Marissa/Evelyn: schedule a 30‑minute kickoff with NetOps + Security tomorrow 10:00am PT. Evelyn, please send calendar invite and include the Drive diagram and the attachments I shared.

We’ll use the canary plan Rishi suggested. If Jordan approves the temporary tunnel we’ll do the staged test mid‑week.

Marissa
